1.description: Male cardinals beginning to sing territorial songs from high perches, staking out breeding territory early
1.childFriendlyNote: A bright red bird sits on the tippy-top of a tree and sings "birdy birdy birdy" over and over!

1.description: Carolina wrens singing year-round from brush piles and garden sheds, loud for their tiny size
1.childFriendlyNote: A tiny rusty-brown bird shouts "teakettle teakettle teakettle" so loud it makes you jump!

1.description: Holly trees loaded with bright red berries against glossy dark green leaves, feeding winter birds
1.childFriendlyNote: Shiny red berries on spiky green leaves, like nature's own Christmas decorations that birds love to eat

1.description: Barred owls calling "who cooks for you, who cooks for you all" in bottomland woods at dusk
1.childFriendlyNote: After dark, listen for a deep hoot that sounds like someone asking "who cooks for you?"

1.description: Evergreen Christmas ferns still green on woodland slopes, one of the few green things in the winter forest
1.childFriendlyNote: These tough green ferns stay green even when everything else is brown and bare. Feel how leathery the leaves are!

2.description: Male cardinals singing louder and more frequently as days lengthen, bright red against bare winter branches
2.childFriendlyNote: That bright red bird is singing even louder now. He wants everyone to know this is his tree!

2.description: Witch hazel blooming with spidery yellow ribbons on bare branches, one of the very first flowers of the year
2.childFriendlyNote: Crinkly yellow ribbons burst from bare branches. This brave little tree blooms when everything else is asleep!

2.description: Chickadees visiting feeders in small flocks, calling their buzzy "chick-a-dee-dee-dee"
2.childFriendlyNote: A tiny grey bird with a black cap hangs upside down and calls its own name: "chick-a-dee-dee-dee!"

2.description: Mosses on rocks and tree bases are lush and green after winter rains, soft emerald cushions in the grey forest
2.childFriendlyNote: Soft green pillows growing on rocks and tree roots. Press gently and feel how spongy and damp they are!

2.description: Mistletoe clumps clearly visible as green balls high in bare deciduous trees, especially oaks
2.childFriendlyNote: Look up at the bare trees. See those round green clumps way up high? That's mistletoe growing right on the branches!

3.description: Red maple buds swelling and turning deep red, some of the earliest tree buds to break in late winter
3.childFriendlyNote: The tips of the maple branches are turning red, like tiny red dots getting ready to pop open!

3.description: Tufted titmice calling "peter peter peter" from treetops, beginning to form breeding pairs
3.childFriendlyNote: A grey bird with a pointy mohawk whistles "peter peter peter". It sounds like it's calling a friend!

3.description: Carolina wrens exploring nest sites in sheds, mailboxes, and hanging planters
3.childFriendlyNote: These cheeky little birds poke into flowerpots and old boots looking for a place to build a nest!

3.description: Pine warblers singing trilling songs from high in pine trees, one of the few warblers that overwinters
3.childFriendlyNote: Up in the tall pine trees, a yellow-green bird sings a buzzy trill. It stayed here all winter while other birds flew south!

3.description: Barred owls actively courting and nesting, dueting calls echoing through bottomland forests
3.childFriendlyNote: Two owls call back and forth in the dark woods, "who cooks for you?" "who cooks for you?" They're a couple!

4.description: Red maple flowers opening, tiny red clusters giving a rosy haze to swamp edges and woodland canopies
4.childFriendlyNote: Squint at the treetops. The maples look like they're blushing pink! Tiny red flowers are opening before the leaves come

4.description: Skunk cabbage hoods pushing through mud in mountain wetlands, generating their own heat to melt through frozen ground
4.childFriendlyNote: A weird purple hood pokes out of the swampy mud. Sniff carefully and yuck! It smells like a skunk! That's its name!

4.description: Cardinals singing at dawn, males chasing rivals along territory boundaries
4.childFriendlyNote: The red bird wakes you up singing before the sun is even all the way up!

4.description: Wintering white-throated sparrows singing sweet whistled songs from brush piles before heading north
4.childFriendlyNote: A stripey sparrow whistles a sad sweet tune from the bushes, "oh sweet Canada Canada Canada". It's dreaming of home!

4.description: Daffodil shoots emerging from garden beds and old homesites, green spears pushing through mulch
4.childFriendlyNote: Green swords are poking out of the ground. They're daffodils getting ready to show off their yellow flowers!

5.description: Red maple flowers in full bloom, tiny red clusters attract early pollinators on warm afternoons
5.childFriendlyNote: The maple trees are covered in fuzzy red flowers. Bees are already visiting them on warm days!

5.description: Henbit blooming purple in lawns and garden edges, one of the earliest spring wildflowers
5.childFriendlyNote: Tiny purple flowers are popping up in the grass. Look closely and they look like little hoods with tongues sticking out!

5.description: Flocks of robins foraging on lawns and in berry-laden trees, some overwintered locally
5.childFriendlyNote: Robins with orange bellies are hopping across the grass, tilting their heads to listen for worms underground!

5.description: Bluebird pairs inspecting nest boxes and natural cavities, beginning to stake out territories
5.childFriendlyNote: A brilliant blue bird sits on a fence post. It's checking out birdhouses to pick the perfect home!

5.description: Witch hazel flowers fading as other early bloomers take over, spidery yellow petals curling
5.childFriendlyNote: The crinkly yellow ribbons on the witch hazel are starting to shrivel up. Their job is done!

6.description: Early daffodils opening bright yellow trumpets in gardens, old homesites, and roadsides
6.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow trumpets are opening everywhere. The daffodils are blowing their horns to say spring is coming!

6.description: Purple, yellow, and white crocuses blooming in lawns and garden beds, attracting early bees
6.childFriendlyNote: Little purple and yellow cups pop open in the sunshine and close when it gets cloudy. They're solar powered!

6.description: Red-shouldered hawks calling loud "kee-aah" from woodland edges, soaring in courtship displays
6.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk screams "kee-aah!" from the treetops. It sounds fierce but it's just saying hello to its sweetheart!

6.description: Bluebird pairs actively claiming nest boxes, male perching on top and singing soft warbles
6.childFriendlyNote: The blue bird sits on top of his birdhouse singing quietly. He's so proud of his new home!

6.description: Star chickweed blooming white in woodland edges, each petal deeply split to look like ten petals
6.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white stars scattered on the forest floor. Each flower looks like it has ten petals but it's a trick, it only has five split in half!

7.description: Daffodils in peak bloom along roadsides, in old cemeteries, and garden beds
7.childFriendlyNote: Fields of golden trumpets nodding in the breeze. Daffodils are having a party and everyone's invited!

7.description: First spring peepers calling from ponds and wet areas on warm evenings, a high-pitched "peep peep peep"
7.childFriendlyNote: On a warm night, listen near a pond. Hundreds of tiny frogs smaller than your thumb are peeping as loud as they can!

7.description: Callery pear trees bursting into white bloom along streets and parking lots, strong unpleasant smell
7.childFriendlyNote: Those trees covered in white flowers smell kind of stinky. Hold your nose and enjoy the pretty blossoms!

7.description: Purple deadnettle carpeting bare ground in gardens and fields, purple-tipped fuzzy leaves
7.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy purple plants are taking over bare patches of dirt. Touch the soft leaves and don't worry, they don't sting at all!

7.description: Red maple flowers fading, tiny winged seeds (samaras) developing, still reddish
7.childFriendlyNote: The maple's red flowers are turning into tiny helicopter seeds. Soon they'll spin down like little propellers!

8.description: Spring peepers calling in full chorus from every pond and ditch on warm evenings, deafening up close
8.childFriendlyNote: Stand by a pond at sunset and the peeping is so loud you can barely hear your friend talk, all from frogs the size of a grape!

8.description: Serviceberry blooming white on woodland edges, delicate star-shaped flowers before leaves emerge
8.childFriendlyNote: A small tree on the edge of the woods is covered in white stars. It blooms so early the bees are thrilled!

8.description: Daffodils still going strong, later varieties opening as early ones begin to fade
8.childFriendlyNote: Some daffodils are fading but new ones keep opening. It's like a relay race of yellow flowers!

8.description: Wood frogs breeding in mountain vernal pools, clucking calls like ducks, egg masses visible
8.childFriendlyNote: In puddles in the woods, brown frogs that look like they're wearing a mask are quacking like tiny ducks!

8.description: Redbud flower buds swelling along branches and even on the trunk, getting ready for a spectacular show
8.childFriendlyNote: Little pink bumps are covering the branches of a grey tree. Get ready, something amazing is about to happen!

9.description: Redbud trees beginning to bloom, magenta-pink flowers erupting directly from branches and trunk
9.childFriendlyNote: Pink flowers are bursting right out of the bark! The tree is so excited for spring it grows flowers on its own trunk!

9.description: Spring peepers in massive choruses, calling all night long from wetlands and pond edges
9.childFriendlyNote: The frog chorus is so loud tonight you can hear it through closed windows, peep peep peep all night long!

9.description: Carolina jessamine vines draped in golden-yellow trumpet flowers along fences and up into trees
9.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpets hang from vines climbing up trees and fences. It smells sweet but remember, look don't taste!

9.description: Bluebirds actively nest-building, carrying grass and pine needles into nest boxes
9.childFriendlyNote: Watch the bluebird fly to the nest box with a beak full of grass. It's decorating its new bedroom!

9.description: Flowering quince shrubs covered in red, pink, or coral blossoms in gardens and hedgerows
9.childFriendlyNote: A thorny bush is covered in bright red flowers like little roses. Spring is really showing off now!

9.description: Dandelions blooming yellow in lawns and fields, early pollinators grateful for easy nectar
9.childFriendlyNote: Sunny yellow circles are popping up all over the grass. Bees love them even if grown-ups don't!

10.description: Redbud in peak bloom, entire trees glowing magenta-pink against still-bare woods, flowers edible
10.childFriendlyNote: The whole tree is glowing pink! No leaves yet, just thousands of tiny pink flowers covering every branch

10.description: Dogwood flower buds swelling and starting to crack open, showing white or pink bracts inside
10.childFriendlyNote: The dogwood buds look like tiny wrapped presents. They're just starting to unwrap their white petals!

10.description: Spring peepers still calling strongly from ponds and wet meadows every evening
10.childFriendlyNote: The tiny frogs are still having their nightly concert. Close your eyes and the pond sounds like a thousand tiny bells!

10.description: Forsythia shrubs blazing golden yellow along yards and roadsides, flowers before leaves
10.childFriendlyNote: Big bushes have turned completely yellow like giant popcorn. It's like they caught sunshine and held onto it!

10.description: Robins building mud-lined nests in trees and on porches, pulling earthworms from damp lawns
10.childFriendlyNote: Watch the robin run across the grass, stop, tilt its head, then yank out a worm. Dinner is served!

10.description: Wild violets blooming purple and white in lawns, woodland edges, and shady garden corners
10.childFriendlyNote: Tiny purple faces peek up from the grass. Each violet looks like it's smiling at you!

11.description: Redbud still in peak bloom at higher elevations, lowland trees starting to leaf out alongside fading flowers
11.childFriendlyNote: The redbud is still going strong. Now it has pink flowers and baby green leaves at the same time!

11.description: Dogwood bracts opening, white or pink four-petaled flowers appearing at woodland edges
11.childFriendlyNote: The dogwood is unwrapping! Four big white petals open up with a tiny green button in the middle

11.description: Wild azaleas beginning to bloom pink and white along streams and forest edges, sweet honeysuckle scent
11.childFriendlyNote: Pink and white flowers glow in the shady woods. Lean in and take a deep breath of the sweetest smell!

11.description: First ruby-throated hummingbirds arriving from Central America, scouts appearing at feeders and flowers
11.childFriendlyNote: A tiny jewel with a buzzing sound zooms past. The hummingbird just flew all the way across the ocean to get here!

11.description: Spring beauty wildflowers carpeting woodland floors, pink-striped white petals closing on cloudy days
11.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is covered in tiny pink-striped flowers. They close up when clouds come and open again in sunshine!

12.description: Dogwood approaching peak bloom, iconic white and pink bracts lighting up woodland understory
12.childFriendlyNote: The woods are full of floating white flowers. Dogwood trees look like they're holding hundreds of butterflies!

12.description: Redbud flowers fading to papery pink as heart-shaped leaves emerge, seed pods beginning to form
12.childFriendlyNote: The redbud's pink flowers are fading but look. Adorable heart-shaped leaves are taking their place!

12.description: Spring peeper chorus fading as breeding season winds down, still audible on warm evenings
12.childFriendlyNote: The peeping chorus is getting quieter now. The little frogs are finishing their spring singing

12.description: Wild azaleas in full bloom along streams and mountain slopes, clouds of pink in the understory
12.childFriendlyNote: The woods smell like perfume! Pink azalea flowers are everywhere, like cotton candy growing on bushes

12.description: First tiger swallowtail butterflies appearing on warm days, big yellow wings with black stripes
12.childFriendlyNote: A huge yellow butterfly with black tiger stripes floats past. It's as big as your hand!

12.description: Pine pollen clouds released on windy days, coating everything in yellow-green dust, cars and puddles turned yellow
12.childFriendlyNote: Everything outside is covered in yellow dust. Run your finger along a car and it's bright yellow! That's tree pollen

13.description: Dogwood in peak bloom at all elevations, the signature spring tree of the Southeast
13.childFriendlyNote: Everywhere you look, dogwood trees are showing off their white and pink flowers. It's the biggest party in the woods!

13.description: Wisteria vines cascading purple-violet flower clusters over fences, trees, and abandoned buildings
13.childFriendlyNote: Purple waterfalls are dripping from the trees! Wisteria flowers hang down like bunches of grapes made of lavender

13.description: More hummingbirds arriving daily, visiting feeders and red tubular flowers, males flashing ruby throat
13.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird hovers in front of a red flower and its throat flashes ruby red like a tiny jewel!

13.description: Green treefrogs beginning to call from pond edges and rain gardens, "quank quank quank" on rainy evenings
13.childFriendlyNote: After rain, listen for a loud "quank quank quank" near water. It's a bright green frog the color of a lime!

13.description: Wild violets in peak bloom, purple patches in every shady lawn and woodland edge
13.childFriendlyNote: Purple violets are everywhere in the grass. Pick one and look closely at the tiny purple stripes inside

14.description: Dogwood flowers still glorious, bracts turning slightly pink with age, leaves unfurling beneath
14.childFriendlyNote: The dogwood flowers are blushing pink at the edges as they get older. Even fading flowers are beautiful!

14.description: Wisteria in full bloom, heavy purple clusters weighing down arbors and draped over everything
14.childFriendlyNote: The purple wisteria smells so sweet. Stand underneath and look up through a ceiling of purple flowers!

14.description: Garden azaleas exploding in every color (pink, white, coral, magenta), the iconic Southern spring shrub
14.childFriendlyNote: Bushes explode with so many flowers you can't even see the leaves, pink, white, red, like nature's fireworks!

14.description: Tiger swallowtails now common, big yellow-and-black butterflies visiting azaleas and garden flowers
14.childFriendlyNote: Giant yellow butterflies with little tails flutter from flower to flower. They love the azaleas!

14.description: Green treefrogs calling regularly on warm rainy evenings, choruses building
14.childFriendlyNote: The green frogs are getting louder every night, quank quank quank like a hundred tiny ducks!

14.description: Red buckeye blooming with upright red flower clusters in woodland understory, hummingbird magnet
14.childFriendlyNote: Red candles of flowers stand up on a small tree. Watch hummingbirds zoom in for a sip!

15.description: Wisteria still blooming but petals starting to fall like purple rain
15.childFriendlyNote: Purple petals drift down like confetti. Stand under the wisteria and let them land on your head!

15.description: Hummingbirds fully established, defending flower patches and feeders aggressively
15.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird sits on a tiny branch and chases away any other bird that comes near its flowers, so fierce for something so small!

15.description: Wild blackberry canes covered in white five-petaled flowers along roadsides and woodland edges
15.childFriendlyNote: White flowers cover the prickly brambles. Each flower is a promise of a juicy blackberry later this summer!

15.description: Chimney swifts returned from South America, twittering overhead in erratic flight, "flying cigars"
15.childFriendlyNote: Look up! Little birds shaped like boomerangs zip and chatter overhead. They never land on branches, only on walls!

15.description: Native dwarf iris blooming lavender-blue on woodland slopes and shaded rock outcrops
15.childFriendlyNote: Tiny purple-blue flowers with fuzzy yellow landing strips. They're like little airports for bees!

16.description: Azaleas still in peak glory, later varieties opening in deeper colors
16.childFriendlyNote: The azalea bushes are still going. Now the deep pink and red ones are joining the party!

16.description: Blackberry in full flower, bumblebees working every bloom, green berries beginning to form
16.childFriendlyNote: Fat fuzzy bees are rolling around in the blackberry flowers. They're covered in yellow dust!

16.description: Male indigo buntings arriving and singing from power lines and treetops, electric blue in sunlight
16.childFriendlyNote: A bird as blue as a sapphire sits on a wire and sings and sings. It just flew here from Mexico!

16.description: Box turtles emerging from winter dormancy, crossing paths and roads on warm rainy days
16.childFriendlyNote: A little orange and brown turtle slowly crosses the path. It carries its house on its back and can close up like a box!

16.description: Tulip poplar trees blooming with green-and-orange tulip-shaped flowers high in the canopy
16.childFriendlyNote: Way up high, one of the tallest trees has flowers shaped like real tulips. Look for fallen ones on the ground!

16.description: Five-lined skinks basking on warm rocks and fences, young ones with electric-blue tails
16.childFriendlyNote: A little lizard with a bright blue tail does push-ups on a warm rock. The blue tail is to trick birds into grabbing the wrong end!

17.description: Southern magnolia flower buds swelling, large fuzzy buds visible among glossy evergreen leaves
17.childFriendlyNote: Big fuzzy buds the size of eggs are getting ready to pop. The magnolia is saving its best surprise!

17.description: Mockingbirds singing complex songs from rooftops and treetops, sometimes singing through the night
17.childFriendlyNote: This grey bird sings a different song every few seconds. It copies cardinals, jays, even car alarms!

17.description: Box turtles now fully active, foraging for mushrooms, berries, and insects in leaf litter
17.childFriendlyNote: The box turtle munches on a mushroom like it's the most delicious thing in the world, crunch crunch crunch!

17.description: Chimney swifts twittering overhead in growing numbers, catching insects on the wing all day long
17.childFriendlyNote: The sky is full of chattering boomerang birds snapping up bugs. They eat while they fly!

17.description: Honeysuckle vines blooming on fences and woodland edges, intoxicating sweet scent fills the air
17.childFriendlyNote: Close your eyes and breathe in. That amazing sweet smell is honeysuckle! Pull out the tiny string inside for a drop of nectar

18.description: First magnolia flowers opening, enormous creamy white saucers with a lemony sweet fragrance
18.childFriendlyNote: A flower as big as a dinner plate opens on the magnolia tree. Lean in and smell lemons and vanilla!

18.description: First fireflies blinking over lawns and meadows at dusk, just a few scouts on warm humid evenings
18.childFriendlyNote: As it gets dark, tiny lights blink on and off in the grass. The fireflies are waking up!

18.description: Honeysuckle in full bloom, the sweet heavy scent drifting on warm evening air
18.childFriendlyNote: The honeysuckle smells so sweet you can smell it from far away. Gently pull the thread inside a flower for a tiny drop of honey!

18.description: Copperheads active and well-camouflaged in leaf litter, watch where you step on woodland trails
18.childFriendlyNote: Look before you step on leaves! A copper-colored snake with hourglass patterns hides there. Stay back and admire from far away

18.description: Green blackberry fruits forming where flowers were, still hard and sour
18.childFriendlyNote: Little green bumpy balls are growing where the white flowers were. They'll turn into blackberries but don't eat them yet, they're super sour!

18.description: Brown thrashers singing from treetops, repeating each phrase twice, the state bird of Georgia
18.childFriendlyNote: A rusty-red bird sings every song twice, "tweet tweet, chirp chirp, trill trill", like it wants to make sure you heard!

19.description: More magnolia flowers opening, fragrance heavy on warm humid evenings
19.childFriendlyNote: Giant white flowers glow on the magnolia tree like moons. Each one only lasts a few days before turning brown

19.description: Fireflies increasing in numbers, blinking yellow-green over lawns and meadow edges at dusk
19.childFriendlyNote: More and more tiny lights float up from the grass as darkness falls. Each one is a beetle with a glowing bottom!

19.description: Unmated male mockingbirds singing through the night under streetlights, dozens of different songs
19.childFriendlyNote: That bird singing at midnight? It's a mockingbird who hasn't found a girlfriend yet. He sings all night hoping she'll hear!

19.description: Black swallowtail butterflies visiting gardens, females laying eggs on parsley, dill, and fennel
19.childFriendlyNote: A black butterfly with yellow spots flutters around the herb garden. She's looking for parsley to lay her eggs on!

19.description: Kudzu vines growing explosively, covering trees, power poles, and abandoned structures at visible speed
19.childFriendlyNote: This vine grows so fast you can almost watch it happen. It swallows whole trees and makes spooky green shapes!

20.description: Firefly numbers building, warm humid evenings bring dozens of blinking lights over lawns and meadows
20.childFriendlyNote: The yard is full of blinking lights! Each firefly flash is a love letter. They're writing messages to each other!

20.description: Magnolia flowers appearing regularly, large creamy blooms contrasting with dark glossy leaves
20.childFriendlyNote: The magnolia tree has so many huge white flowers it looks like it's decorated for a wedding!

20.description: Elderberry bushes covered in flat white flower clusters along roadsides and stream banks
20.childFriendlyNote: Big flat plates of tiny white flowers sit on top of the bushes like nature's dinner plates!

20.description: Young garden spiders beginning to build small webs in garden edges and tall grass
20.childFriendlyNote: Tiny spiders are building their first webs between plants. Come back in summer to see them grow huge!

20.description: Honeysuckle flowers turning from white to yellow as they age, still fragrant
20.childFriendlyNote: The honeysuckle flowers turn yellow as they get old. White ones are young and yellow ones are growing up!

21.description: Firefly display at or near peak, magical evening light shows over lawns, fields, and woodland clearings
21.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny lanterns float over the grass like fairy lights. This is the best time to watch fireflies!

21.description: First annual cicadas beginning to buzz from treetops on the hottest afternoons
21.childFriendlyNote: On a hot afternoon, a loud buzzing starts in the trees. It's a big bug called a cicada turning up its volume!

21.description: Butterfly weed blooming bright orange along roadsides and in meadows, attracting swallowtails
21.childFriendlyNote: Bright orange flowers that butterflies can't resist. They crowd onto the flowers like kids at an ice cream truck!

21.description: First blackberries turning red then black along roadsides and hedgerows, earliest ones ripening
21.childFriendlyNote: Some blackberries are turning from red to purple-black. If they're black and fall right into your hand, they're ready to eat!

21.description: Hummingbirds visiting trumpet creeper, bee balm, and feeders constantly, territorial battles escalating
21.childFriendlyNote: Two hummingbirds chase each other around the garden like tiny helicopters having a dogfight!

22.description: Fireflies still putting on magnificent evening shows, peak display continuing
22.childFriendlyNote: Go outside at dusk and it's like the grass is full of stars. The fireflies are still dancing!

22.description: Crepe myrtle trees beginning to bloom in pink, purple, red, and white, ruffled flower clusters
22.childFriendlyNote: Trees along the street burst into pink and purple. Touch the crinkly flowers, they feel like tissue paper!

22.description: Blackberries ripening fast in the heat, dark purple-black fruit hanging heavy on thorny canes
22.childFriendlyNote: Blackberries are ripe! Pick the dark ones gently. Watch out for thorns and try not to get purple fingers... too late!

22.description: Green treefrogs calling loudly on rainy evenings, sometimes found on windows near porch lights
22.childFriendlyNote: Check the window at night. A little green frog might be stuck right on the glass, catching bugs near the light!

22.description: Orange daylilies blooming along roadsides and old homesites, each flower lasts only one day
22.childFriendlyNote: Orange flowers line the road like traffic cones. Each one only opens for one day and then a new one takes its turn!

23.description: Cicadas buzzing louder from treetops, the soundtrack of Southern summer afternoons
23.childFriendlyNote: The trees are buzzing so loud on hot days. Look for the empty cicada shells clinging to tree bark like tiny robot suits!

23.description: Crepe myrtle in full bloom, clouds of ruffled flowers topping every tree in shades of pink and purple
23.childFriendlyNote: Whole streets are lined with pink and purple pom-pom trees. Crepe myrtles are the queen of Southern summer!

23.description: Firefly numbers starting to decline but still visible on warm humid evenings
23.childFriendlyNote: The fireflies aren't quite as many now but you can still see their twinkle-lights at bedtime

23.description: Lantana blooming in gardens and along roads, multi-colored flower clusters attracting butterflies
23.childFriendlyNote: One bush has flowers that are pink, orange, and yellow all at once. Butterflies can't decide which color to visit first!

23.description: Hummingbirds nesting and visiting trumpet vine, bee balm, and salvias constantly
23.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird sticks its long beak deep into a red trumpet flower and drinks like using a straw!

24.description: Cicada chorus deafening on hot afternoons, empty nymph shells on tree trunks everywhere
24.childFriendlyNote: Peel a crunchy cicada shell off a tree trunk. It's just the empty suit the bug left behind when it grew wings!

24.description: Crepe myrtles in full spectacular bloom, the defining summer tree of the Southeast
24.childFriendlyNote: Every yard has a crepe myrtle tree covered in crinkly flowers. Pick up a fallen petal and feel how papery it is!

24.description: Trumpet vine blooming orange-red on fences and dead trees, hummingbird's favorite native flower
24.childFriendlyNote: Orange trumpet flowers hang like bells on the fence. Watch a hummingbird poke its face right inside one!

24.description: Afternoon thunderstorms building daily, dramatic cloud towers and lightning, rain bringing relief from heat
24.childFriendlyNote: Giant clouds pile up like mountains in the sky, then boom, thunder and warm rain that smells like wet earth!

24.description: Passionflower vines blooming with intricate purple and white flowers on fences and roadsides
24.childFriendlyNote: The most amazing flower you've ever seen. It looks like an alien spaceship made of purple fringes and curly antennae!

25.description: Peak cicada season, the buzzing rises and falls in waves through the trees on scorching afternoons
25.childFriendlyNote: The buzzing gets louder and louder and louder then suddenly stops. Then it starts all over again!

25.description: Passionflower in peak bloom, intricate flowers with wavy purple filaments and green fruit forming
25.childFriendlyNote: Each passionflower has a crazy crown of purple strings. Look for the green egg-shaped fruits growing too!

25.description: Yellow garden spiders now large and conspicuous, building zigzag webs between garden plants
25.childFriendlyNote: A big yellow-and-black spider sits in the middle of a huge web with a zigzag stripe. She wrote her name in silk!

25.description: Katydids beginning to call "katy-did katy-didn't" from treetops on warm evenings
25.childFriendlyNote: At night the trees argue back and forth ("Katy did!" "Katy didn't!") it's green leaf-shaped insects having a debate!

25.description: Black-eyed Susans blooming golden yellow with dark centers in meadows and roadsides
25.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow flowers with a chocolate button in the middle. They look like tiny sunflowers wearing sunglasses!

26.description: Cicadas still the dominant summer sound, buzzing through the hottest hours
26.childFriendlyNote: It's so hot and the cicadas are so loud. Summer is really showing off right now!

26.description: Crepe myrtles continuing their long bloom, spent flowers dropping papery petals
26.childFriendlyNote: Pink petals fall like tiny crinkly snowflakes under the crepe myrtle. Scoop some up and toss them!

26.description: Katydids now calling regularly, adding their voice to the chorus of cicadas and tree crickets at night
26.childFriendlyNote: The nighttime sounds are amazing, katydids and crickets and frogs all singing together like a bug orchestra!

26.description: Trumpet vine still blooming profusely, hummingbirds visiting every few minutes
26.childFriendlyNote: The orange trumpet flowers are still going strong. Sit quietly and count how many times a hummingbird visits in five minutes!

26.description: Muscadine grapes developing on wild vines, still green and hard, clusters dangling from trees
26.childFriendlyNote: Green grape balls hang from vines climbing up the trees. They'll turn purple later and the raccoons love them!

27.description: Peak summer heat brings peak cicada volume, their buzzing seems to make the air vibrate
27.childFriendlyNote: The cicadas are so loud it's like the trees have speakers! Can you feel the buzz vibrating in your chest?

27.description: Crepe myrtles in full midsummer glory, blooms lasting for weeks in the heat
27.childFriendlyNote: The crepe myrtles just keep blooming and blooming: pink, purple, and white pom-poms everywhere you look!

27.description: Hummingbirds at peak activity, adults and fledglings visiting every red tubular flower and feeder
27.childFriendlyNote: Baby hummingbirds are learning to hover! They're a bit wobbly, not as smooth as their parents yet

27.description: Queen Anne's lace blooming white in meadows and roadsides, flat flower heads like tiny doilies
27.childFriendlyNote: White lacy flowers like tiny umbrellas line the road. Look for the single purple dot in the very center!

27.description: Skinks basking and hunting on warm rocks, walls, and patios in the summer heat
27.childFriendlyNote: A quick little lizard does lightning-fast push-ups on the warm stones. Blink and you'll miss it zoom away!

28.description: Cicada choruses continue, find shed exoskeletons clinging to tree bark
28.childFriendlyNote: Collect the crunchy brown cicada shells from tree bark. They're hollow! The bug crawled out of its own back!

28.description: Joe-Pye weed beginning to bloom tall dusty-pink flower clusters, towering above other meadow plants
28.childFriendlyNote: A plant taller than a grown-up has big fuzzy pink flower heads on top. Butterflies line up to visit!

28.description: Ironweed blooming vivid purple in meadows and along streams, one of the richest purple wildflowers
28.childFriendlyNote: The most electric purple flowers stand tall in the field. The color is so bright it almost glows!

28.description: Large female garden spiders at peak size, impressive webs strung with morning dew
28.childFriendlyNote: Early morning is magic time. The spider web is covered in tiny water drops that sparkle like diamonds!

28.description: Hummingbirds visiting feeders frantically, beginning to bulk up for fall migration
28.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbirds are eating like crazy. They're getting chubby because they have a very long trip coming up!

29.description: Early goldenrod species beginning to bloom golden yellow along roadsides and field edges
29.childFriendlyNote: Golden yellow plumes are starting to wave from the roadsides. Goldenrod doesn't make you sneeze, that's ragweed's fault!

29.description: Katydid chorus at full volume on warm nights, calling continuously from dusk till dawn
29.childFriendlyNote: Fall asleep to the katydids arguing all night long ("Katy did!" "Katy didn't!") they never agree!

29.description: Cicadas still buzzing strongly, their sound now mixed with the evening cricket and katydid chorus
29.childFriendlyNote: Daytime belongs to the cicadas, nighttime belongs to the katydids. They take turns being loud!

29.description: Hummingbird activity intensifying at feeders as birds fatten up before crossing the Gulf of Mexico
29.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird drinks and drinks and drinks. It needs to double its weight to fly across the whole ocean!

29.description: Persimmon fruits visible but still hard and green on the tree, extremely astringent if tasted
29.childFriendlyNote: Green balls hang from a tree. They're persimmons but don't taste them yet, your whole mouth will pucker up like a fish face!

30.description: Goldenrod blooming more abundantly, golden plumes attracting soldier beetles and butterflies
30.childFriendlyNote: Fields of gold! The goldenrod is like sunshine growing from the ground. Bees and butterflies love it!

30.description: Local monarch butterflies visiting milkweed and garden flowers, still breeding not yet migrating
30.childFriendlyNote: An orange butterfly with black lines floats by like a stained-glass window come to life. It's a monarch!

30.description: Spider webs spectacular with heavy morning dew, every fence and garden bush draped in glistening silk
30.childFriendlyNote: Wake up early and the whole garden is draped in sparkling spider silk. Each web is a tiny jeweled net!

30.description: Hummingbirds feeding almost non-stop at flowers and feeders, storing fat for migration
30.childFriendlyNote: Count how many times the hummingbird visits the feeder in one hour. It might be more than 50!

30.description: Joe-Pye weed in full bloom, tall dusty-pink flower heads attracting swallowtails and monarchs
30.childFriendlyNote: These giant pink flowers are a butterfly buffet. Watch swallowtails and monarchs share the table!

31.description: Goldenrod in full peak bloom, roadsides and meadows glowing golden, buzzing with pollinators
31.childFriendlyNote: The goldenrod is so golden it makes the whole meadow glow. Lean close and hear the happy humming of bees!

31.description: Early hummingbirds beginning to depart southward, activity at feeders seems even higher with migrants passing through
31.childFriendlyNote: Some hummingbirds are already leaving! They'll fly 500 miles across the ocean without stopping. Go little bird, go!

31.description: Cicadas still calling but noticeably fewer as summer slowly wanes
31.childFriendlyNote: The cicada buzz is a little quieter now. Summer is starting to think about wrapping up

31.description: Persimmon fruits turning orange-ish but still not ripe, hanging like ornaments on the tree
31.childFriendlyNote: The persimmons are turning orange but they're still not ready. Patience! The frost has to come first

31.description: Crepe myrtles still blooming but first clusters fading, some varieties on second flush of flowers
31.childFriendlyNote: The crepe myrtles are still going. Some flowers are fading but new ones keep popping up. They never quit!

32.description: Goldenrod still in spectacular bloom, dominant wildflower of late summer meadows
32.childFriendlyNote: The golden fields are buzzing like a city. Every insect in the world seems to be visiting the goldenrod!

32.description: Monarch butterflies beginning to move southward, nectaring on goldenrod and asters along the way
32.childFriendlyNote: The orange monarchs are heading south to Mexico. Some of them have to fly over 2,000 miles! What a trip!

32.description: Hummingbird numbers dropping as migration picks up, treasure every sighting
32.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbirds are saying goodbye. Wave as they zoom past on their way to Central America!

32.description: Field crickets chirping from grass and leaf litter, the tempo slowing as nighttime temperatures drop
32.childFriendlyNote: Crickets chirp faster when it's warm and slower when it's cool. They're like little living thermometers!

32.description: Muscadine grapes beginning to ripen, turning bronze or purple, musky sweet scent on warm days
32.childFriendlyNote: Wild grapes hanging from vines are turning purple. They smell sweet and grapey and the possums eat them at night!

33.description: Goldenrod still dominant but some species starting to fade, later varieties taking over
33.childFriendlyNote: The golden meadow is still glowing. New kinds of goldenrod are blooming as the earlier ones rest

33.description: More monarchs passing through on southward migration, sometimes gathering in overnight roosts
33.childFriendlyNote: Watch for orange butterflies all heading the same direction. They're following an invisible highway to Mexico!

33.description: Last hummingbirds passing through on migration, keep feeders up through September
33.childFriendlyNote: Don't take the feeder down yet! Late hummingbirds are still stopping for one last drink before their big journey

33.description: Ironweed still blooming vivid purple, standing tall above fading summer wildflowers
33.childFriendlyNote: The ironweed's purple is fading a bit but it's still the tallest, proudest flower in the field

33.description: Katydids still calling at night but the chorus is noticeably thinner as some individuals die off
33.childFriendlyNote: The katydid debate is getting quieter, fewer voices in the nighttime choir each week

34.description: Monarch migration in full swing, butterflies nectaring heavily on goldenrod and asters for fuel
34.childFriendlyNote: The monarchs are really moving now. Some fly 50 miles a day! Watch them fuel up on flowers like tiny airplanes

34.description: Earlier goldenrod species fading to fluffy seed heads, later species still golden
34.childFriendlyNote: Some goldenrod is turning fluffy and white like tiny clouds. The seeds are getting ready to fly away on the wind!

34.description: Wild asters beginning to bloom blue, purple, and white along roadsides and woodland edges
34.childFriendlyNote: Purple and blue daisy-like flowers are opening everywhere. They're called asters and they're fall's favorite flower!

34.description: Heavy morning dew reveals dozens of spider webs in every garden and meadow, jeweled with droplets
34.childFriendlyNote: Every bush and fence has a spider web covered in tiny diamonds. Morning dew turns the whole garden into a jewelry store!

34.description: Muscadine grapes ripe and falling, sweet musky scent drawing deer, raccoons, and opossums
34.childFriendlyNote: Ripe purple grapes litter the ground under the vine. They smell like grape juice and every critter wants some!

35.description: Monarch migration continuing, orange wings drifting through gardens and fields heading southwest
35.childFriendlyNote: More orange butterflies floating by like autumn leaves that fly, safe travels, little monarchs!

35.description: Wild asters now blooming abundantly, blue and purple daisies alongside goldenrod in meadows
35.childFriendlyNote: Purple asters and golden goldenrod together look like a field painted in school colors!

35.description: Cricket song dominates cool evenings, a slower, more melancholy rhythm than midsummer
35.childFriendlyNote: The crickets sing slower now that nights are cooler. Count the chirps in 14 seconds and add 40 to get the temperature!

35.description: First woolly bear caterpillars appearing, crossing sidewalks and roads in their fuzzy black-and-brown bands
35.childFriendlyNote: A fuzzy black and brown caterpillar curls into a ball when you touch it. Legend says it predicts how bad winter will be!

35.description: Persimmon fruits turning deeper orange, some starting to soften on the tree
35.childFriendlyNote: The persimmons are getting more orange every day, almost ripe but still needs more time to get sweet!

36.description: Monarch migration still visible, late-season butterflies nectaring on asters and zinnias
36.childFriendlyNote: A few last monarchs are still passing through. Give them a cheer as they fly to their winter home!

36.description: Asters in full glory, fields and roadsides blue with New England aster and purple with aromatic aster
36.childFriendlyNote: The aster flowers are having their big moment, purple and blue everywhere like the sky fell into the fields!

36.description: Woolly bear caterpillars more common, crossing roads and paths looking for places to hibernate
36.childFriendlyNote: Woolly bears are on the march! Help them cross the sidewalk safely. They need to find a cozy spot for winter

36.description: Pawpaw fruits ripening in mountain coves and creek bottoms, custard-like tropical flavor
36.childFriendlyNote: A lumpy green fruit hides in the shady creek bottom. Inside it tastes like banana pudding! It's called a pawpaw

36.description: Broad-winged hawks beginning to kettle up in thermals, migrating south along mountain ridges
36.childFriendlyNote: Look up! Dozens of hawks circle round and round in a rising spiral of warm air. They're riding a sky elevator south!

37.description: Sourwood trees among the first to turn, deep crimson and burgundy in the mountain woods
37.childFriendlyNote: One tree in the green woods is suddenly turning bright red. The sourwood is the first to dress up for fall!

37.description: Wild asters still blooming strongly, the last great nectar source for migrating butterflies and bees
37.childFriendlyNote: Asters are like a farewell feast. Every bee and butterfly stops for one last slurp before winter!

37.description: Peak hawk migration along the Appalachian ridges, kettles of hundreds of broad-wings spiraling skyward
37.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of hawks spiral up up up in the sky like a hawk tornado. They're all heading south together!

37.description: Persimmon fruits soft and ripe after early cool nights, sweet and honey-like when fully ripe
37.childFriendlyNote: The persimmons are finally squishy and sweet like honey-flavored jam, but only eat the super soft ones!

37.description: Cricket chirping slowing as temperatures drop, a peaceful autumn evening soundtrack
37.childFriendlyNote: The cricket song is getting slower and slower, like a music box winding down for winter

38.description: Sweetgum trees beginning to show fall color, star-shaped leaves turning yellow, orange, red, and purple
38.childFriendlyNote: Star-shaped leaves are turning every color at once: red, purple, orange, yellow, all on the same tree!

38.description: Acorns dropping from oaks, bouncing off roofs and cars, squirrels frantically burying them
38.childFriendlyNote: Acorns bonk off your head if you walk under an oak tree. Squirrels are stuffing their cheeks and burying treasure everywhere!

38.description: Woolly bears still commonly seen crossing paths, curling into fuzzy balls when disturbed
38.childFriendlyNote: The woolly bears curl into perfect fuzzy donuts when they're scared. Gently set them in the grass and watch them unroll!

38.description: Early asters fading but late-season species still producing fresh purple blooms
38.childFriendlyNote: Some asters are going fluffy with seeds but new ones keep blooming. They don't want the flower show to end!

38.description: Bucks rubbing antler velvet off on small trees, scraping bark in preparation for rut
38.childFriendlyNote: Look for small trees with bark scraped off. A deer was rubbing his antlers there to get them battle-ready!

39.description: Red maples turning brilliant scarlet at higher elevations, fall color spreading from mountain peaks downward
39.childFriendlyNote: The mountaintops are on fire with color! Red maples glow like red traffic lights in the forest

39.description: Hickory nuts falling with their thick green husks, cracking open to reveal hard-shelled nuts inside
39.childFriendlyNote: Bonk! Big green balls fall from the hickory tree and split open to show a nut inside. The squirrels race to grab them!

39.description: Goldenrod turning to fluffy white seed heads, silky plumes catching the autumn breeze
39.childFriendlyNote: The golden flowers turned into fluffy white puffs. Blow on them and watch tiny seeds float away like wishes!

39.description: Deer becoming more active as rut approaches, bucks sparring and does moving nervously
39.childFriendlyNote: The deer are restless and running around more than usual. The boy deer are showing off their antlers!

39.description: Witch hazel beginning its fall bloom, spidery yellow flowers appearing as leaves turn yellow and fall
39.childFriendlyNote: This magical tree blooms in fall when everything else is done, yellow ribbons on bare branches, like spring decided to visit again!

40.description: Peak fall color in the mountains, sugar maples blazing orange and gold in the high country
40.childFriendlyNote: The mountains look like they're wearing a crown of gold and orange. This is the best leaf-peeping week up high!

40.description: Sweetgum trees at peak color in lower elevations, every leaf a different shade
40.childFriendlyNote: Collect sweetgum leaves and make a rainbow. Each star-shaped leaf is a different color!

40.description: Acorns still falling heavily, blue jays and squirrels competing for the harvest
40.childFriendlyNote: A blue jay stuffs acorns in its throat pouch like a kid stuffing candy in pockets. It can carry five at once!

40.description: Witch hazel in bloom, yellow spider-web flowers stand out against the orange and red fall backdrop
40.childFriendlyNote: While other trees drop their leaves, witch hazel blooms with crinkly yellow flowers. It does everything backwards!

40.description: Last woolly bears settling into leaf litter and under logs for winter hibernation
40.childFriendlyNote: The woolly bears are tucking themselves into piles of leaves for a long winter nap. Sleep tight, fuzzy friends!

41.description: Tulip poplar leaves turning clear golden yellow, large leaves raining down on breezy days
41.childFriendlyNote: Giant golden leaves the size of your hand flutter down like slow-motion butterflies. Catch one!

41.description: Peak fall color reaching the Piedmont, red maples and sweetgums ablaze in yards and parks
41.childFriendlyNote: Now the lowland towns are on fire with color too: red, orange, gold everywhere you look!

41.description: Deer rut in full swing, bucks chasing does across fields and roads, antlers gleaming
41.childFriendlyNote: Deer with big antlers are running around like they're late for something. Be extra careful near roads!

41.description: Dark-eyed juncos arriving from the mountains and the north, hopping under feeders and in leaf litter
41.childFriendlyNote: Little grey and white birds with pink beaks appear on the ground under feeders. They rode the cold weather down from the mountains!

41.description: Persimmons at peak ripeness after frost, dropping soft and sweet from the tree
41.childFriendlyNote: Squishy orange persimmons fall with a plop. The frost made them as sweet as caramel pudding!

42.description: Oaks turning russet, bronze, and deep red, holding their leaves longer than most other trees
42.childFriendlyNote: The mighty oaks are finally changing. They waited for everyone else to go first, now they glow dark red and brown

42.description: Peak leaf fall, walking through deep crunchy layers of golden, red, and brown leaves
42.childFriendlyNote: Crunch crunch crunch! Kick through piles of leaves and smell that amazing earthy autumn smell!

42.description: Junco flocks established at feeders and in yards, flashing white tail feathers as they hop
42.childFriendlyNote: The juncos flash their white tail feathers like little waving flags as they hop along, peek-a-boo!

42.description: White-throated sparrows returning for winter, sweet whistled song from dense thickets
42.childFriendlyNote: A little brown bird whistles a pretty tune from the bushes: "oh sweet Canada" it sings, missing its summer home up north!

42.description: Beautyberry shrubs loaded with clusters of bright magenta-purple berries along bare stems
42.childFriendlyNote: Whoa. Those berries are the most purple purple you've ever seen! They look like someone painted them with a marker!

43.description: Oaks shedding brown and russet leaves, carpeting the ground but many still clinging to branches
43.childFriendlyNote: Oak leaves rattle in the wind and slowly let go one by one. Some stubborn ones hold on all winter!

43.description: Beautyberry still bright purple along forest edges, mockingbirds and robins eating the berries
43.childFriendlyNote: The amazing purple berries are disappearing fast. The birds discovered the candy store!

43.description: Juncos now common winter residents, small flocks scratching in leaf litter everywhere
43.childFriendlyNote: The juncos kick leaves aside with both feet at once (hop hop scratch!) looking for tiny seeds underneath

43.description: Deer rut continuing, bucks still active and visible, antler rubs fresh on small trees
43.childFriendlyNote: The deer are still acting silly. Watch for them at dawn and dusk, especially near the edge of the woods

43.description: Witch hazel still blooming, one of the last flowers of the year, fragrant yellow ribbons on bare branches
43.childFriendlyNote: The witch hazel is still going! Yellow crinkly flowers on a naked tree. It's the last flower of fall

44.description: Last sweetgum leaves dropping, spiky gumballs littering the ground underfoot
44.childFriendlyNote: Ouch! Spiky brown balls cover the ground under the sweetgum. Walk carefully or wear thick shoes!

44.description: White-throated sparrows now settled in for winter, singing from hedgerows and brush piles
44.childFriendlyNote: The sparrow with the white throat sings its sad pretty song from the bushes. It'll be here all winter!

44.description: Holly berries turning bright red against dark evergreen leaves, becoming more visible as other trees lose leaves
44.childFriendlyNote: Red holly berries glow against shiny dark green leaves. The woods are getting their holiday decorations ready!

44.description: Carolina wrens still singing loudly despite the season, roosting in sheltered spots at night
44.childFriendlyNote: Even in late fall, the little wren shouts "teakettle teakettle!". Nothing makes this bird be quiet!

44.description: Barred owls more audible as leaves fall, their "who cooks for you" echoing through bare woods
44.childFriendlyNote: Without leaves to muffle the sound, you can hear the owl hooting from far away: "who cooks for you?"

45.description: Most deciduous trees now bare, revealing bird nests, mistletoe clumps, and the elegant architecture of branches
45.childFriendlyNote: With the leaves gone you can see everything: old bird nests, squirrel nests, and the beautiful shapes of tree branches!

45.description: Cardinals brilliant against bare branches and grey skies, visiting feeders in pairs
45.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal looks even more red against bare grey branches, like a living ornament on a winter tree!

45.description: Junco flocks active under feeders and along woodland edges, "snowbirds" that signal winter
45.childFriendlyNote: People call juncos "snowbirds" because they show up when it gets cold. They're like little grey winter visitors!

45.description: Christmas ferns standing green and leathery on woodland slopes while everything else has gone brown
45.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas fern stays green when everything else gives up. Tough and leathery, it doesn't mind the cold one bit!

45.description: Red-tailed hawks visible perched on bare treetops and power poles, hunting over open fields
45.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk sits on a bare branch watching the field below. Look for its reddish tail glowing in the sunlight!

46.description: Holly berries bright red and fully ripe, robins and cedar waxwings beginning to feast
46.childFriendlyNote: The holly berries are bright red traffic lights for hungry birds: "Stop here! Free food!"

46.description: Chickadees in active mixed flocks with titmice and nuthatches, working through bare branches
46.childFriendlyNote: A gang of tiny birds hops through the bare trees together. Chickadees, titmice, and nuthatches are best friends!

46.description: Mistletoe clumps prominent in bare deciduous trees, green balls with white berries clearly visible
46.childFriendlyNote: Green clumps with white berries hang in the bare trees like nature's ornaments. That's mistletoe!

46.description: Cedar waxwing flocks arriving, sleek masked birds devouring berries from hollies and cedars
46.childFriendlyNote: A flock of fancy birds with black masks and yellow-tipped tails descends on a berry tree and eats everything!

46.description: White-throated sparrows singing their sweet whistled song from thickets on mild days
46.childFriendlyNote: Even on a chilly day, the sparrow sings its pretty whistle from the bushes, "oh sweet Canada Canada Canada!"

47.description: Barred owls calling more frequently in lengthening evenings, their hoots carry far through bare woods
47.childFriendlyNote: The owl starts hooting earlier now that it gets dark so soon: "who cooks for you, who cooks for you allll?"

47.description: Cedar waxwing flocks roaming from berry tree to berry tree, high thin "seee" calls overhead
47.childFriendlyNote: The waxwing flock swoops in, eats all the berries in minutes, and flies off together. Berry bandits!

47.description: Cardinals gathering at feeders in small groups, bright red males and olive-red females side by side
47.childFriendlyNote: Red dad cardinal and brownish-red mom cardinal sit together on the feeder. They're a matching pair!

47.description: Pine trees standing tall and green among bare deciduous trees, pine straw falling in golden carpet
47.childFriendlyNote: The pine trees are the only ones still wearing their green coats. Golden pine needles carpet the ground like straw

47.description: Mosses lush and green on rocks and logs after fall rains, vivid against brown fallen leaves
47.childFriendlyNote: Bright green moss cushions glow on grey rocks. Everything else is brown but the moss stays happy and green!

48.description: Holly trees festive with red berries, a natural holiday decoration that feeds winter birds
48.childFriendlyNote: Holly berries and shiny green leaves. Nature grew its own holiday wreath!

48.description: Carolina wrens singing boldly even in late November, checking garages and sheds for roost sites
48.childFriendlyNote: The little wren peeks into your garage like it's house-hunting. It wants a warm spot to sleep on cold nights!

48.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring over open fields, easier to spot now that trees are bare
48.childFriendlyNote: The big hawk circles high in the cold blue sky, its red tail catching the light. It can spot a mouse from way up there!

48.description: Downy woodpeckers tapping on bare branches and visiting suet feeders, small black-and-white birds
48.childFriendlyNote: A tiny black-and-white bird hammers on a branch (tap tap tap tap!) looking for bugs hiding in the bark

48.description: First hard frosts turning lawns white in the morning, ice crystals sparkling in early sunlight
48.childFriendlyNote: The grass is wearing a sparkly white coat this morning. Touch it and feel the crunch of tiny ice crystals!

49.description: Mistletoe highly visible in bare trees, traditional holiday decoration harvested from December woods
49.childFriendlyNote: See all those green balls high up in the bare trees? Mistletoe is a plant that lives on other trees. It's a tree parasite!

49.description: Cardinals vivid red against grey winter woods and snowy days, visiting feeders regularly
49.childFriendlyNote: The bright red cardinal on the grey branch looks like it belongs on a holiday card. It's the prettiest winter bird!

49.description: Christmas ferns still green on the forest floor, named because they're green at Christmas time
49.childFriendlyNote: These ferns are called Christmas ferns because they're still green right now. Touch a leaflet, it's shaped like a little stocking!

49.description: Titmice visiting feeders with chickadees, grey crested birds scolding from the branches
49.childFriendlyNote: A grey bird with a little mohawk grabs a sunflower seed and flies off to crack it open on a branch, one seed at a time!

49.description: Barred owls calling in early darkness, nesting pairs beginning courtship vocalizations
49.childFriendlyNote: On a quiet December night, the owl hoots through the bare trees. It's already thinking about having babies!

50.description: Holly trees at peak beauty with bright red berries, the quintessential winter evergreen
50.childFriendlyNote: Holly berries are so red and the leaves so green. Nature made its own Christmas colors!

50.description: Waxwing flocks descending on fruiting trees, stripping holly, privet, and cedar berries
50.childFriendlyNote: A whole flock of masked birds lands on a tree and eats every single berry. Then they all fly to the next tree!

50.description: Chickadees in busy mixed flocks, their "chick-a-dee" calls a reliable winter woodland soundtrack
50.childFriendlyNote: Even on the coldest day, the chickadee hops around cheerfully calling its own name: chick-a-dee-dee-dee!

50.description: Pine siskins visiting feeders in irruption years, streaky brown finches with yellow wing flashes
50.childFriendlyNote: Little streaky birds crowd the feeder and argue over seeds. Look for a flash of yellow on their wings!

50.description: Mosses and lichens vivid green on rocks and tree bark, thriving in the cool damp winter air
50.childFriendlyNote: While big plants sleep, the tiny mosses and lichens are having their best time, green and happy in the winter rain!

51.description: Carolina wrens singing on sunny winter days, roosting in nest boxes and sheltered eaves at night
51.childFriendlyNote: On a sunny winter day, the wren can't help but sing ("teakettle teakettle!") winter can't stop this bird!

51.description: Red-tailed hawks perched prominently on bare trees and power poles, watching for prey in short winter grass
51.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk sits perfectly still on a bare tree, watching watching watching. Then whoosh it dives for lunch!

51.description: Mistletoe with white berries conspicuous in bare treetops, spread by birds who eat the sticky fruit
51.childFriendlyNote: Birds eat the sticky white mistletoe berries and accidentally plant new mistletoe on other trees, bird gardeners!

51.description: Cardinals bright red at feeders, sometimes gathering in groups of 10 or more on winter evenings
51.childFriendlyNote: Imagine ten red cardinals on one bush. They look like red ornaments on a Christmas tree!

51.description: Barred owls calling actively on cold clear nights, courtship duets beginning in earnest
51.childFriendlyNote: Two owls are singing a spooky duet in the dark woods: "who cooks for you?" hoots one, and the other answers back!

52.description: Holly trees glowing with red berries in the winter woods, a vital food source for overwintering birds
52.childFriendlyNote: The holly tree is nature's Christmas gift to the birds, red berries wrapped in shiny green leaves!

52.description: Cardinals the brightest thing in the winter landscape, males singing tentative dawn songs as days start to lengthen
52.childFriendlyNote: The red cardinal sits in a bare tree and starts to sing softly. It can feel that the days are getting just a tiny bit longer!

52.description: Christmas ferns evergreen on woodland slopes, flattened under frost but still vibrantly green
52.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas fern earned its name. On Christmas Day it's still green while everything else is sleeping!

52.description: Barred owls hooting through the long winter nights, their calls echoing through bare bottomland forests
52.childFriendlyNote: On a cold dark evening, the owl asks "who cooks for you?" Maybe it wants an invitation to holiday dinner!

52.description: Low winter sun casting long golden shadows through bare trees, the year's shortest days rich with slanting light
52.childFriendlyNote: The sun hangs so low that shadows stretch super long and everything glows gold. The shortest days have the prettiest light!
